summary: Bernhard Forssman works in linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg under Karl Hoffmann (~1958–1964) and held posts at the University of Marburg (1968–1983) and Erlangen-Nuremberg (1983).

Bernhard Geiger specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at Vienna (Ph.D. 1905), Bonn, Göttingen, Charles University, and Heidelberg, he taught at Vienna (1909–1938), the Asia Institute, and Columbia University (1951–1956).

Indologist Bernhard Hirzel studied at Zurich, the Carolinum, Berlin, Göttingen (Ph.D. ~1832–1833), and Paris, with teachers including Franz Bopp and Antoine-Léonard Chézy. He held reader, docent, and Privatdozent posts at the University of Zurich between 1833 and 1845.

Linguist Bernhard Jülg studied at Heidelberg, Berlin (under Lachmann, Boeckh, Bopp, Petermann, and Schott), and Kiel (Ph.D. ~1847). He served as professor of classical philology at Lviv (1851), Jagiellonian University (1853), and the University of Innsbruck (1863).

Bernhard Karlgren was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics. After studying at Uppsala University (~1907–1915), he held academic posts at Uppsala (~1915–1918) and the University of Gothenburg (~1918–1939).

Indologist and linguist Bernhard Kölver studied at Kiel, Glasgow, Göttingen, Frankfurt (Ph.D. ~1964), and Cologne. He held posts at Cologne (1966–1976), the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (1970–1972), Kiel University (1974–1993), and the University of Leipzig (1993–2001).

Bernie Glassman worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Brooklyn Polytechnic, NYU, and UCLA (Ph.D. ~1970), training under Taizan Maezumi and Koryu Osaka. He founded the Zen Center of Los Angeles and Zen Peacemakers (1980).

Linguist Bert Vaux studied at the University of Chicago (B.A. 1990) and Harvard University (M.A. 1994). He served on the faculty at Harvard (2000–2003), the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (2003–2006), and the University of Cambridge (from 2006; Professor 2021).

Berthe Jansen works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Leiden University (B.A., Ph.D. under Jonathan A. Silk) and Oxford (M.Phil.). Her career includes posts at Heidelberg University (~2015–2016) and Leiden University (2015–2016).

Berthold Delbrück was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Halle and Berlin under August Friedrich Pott, Albrecht Weber, Franz Bopp, and Heymann Steinthal. He held academic posts at Halle (1867–1870) and the University of Jena (1870–1913).

Berthold Laufer worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied in Berlin and Leipzig (Ph.D. ~1897 under August Conrady), later holding posts at the American Museum of Natural History, Columbia University, and Field Museum of Natural History.

Bertram Fulke Hartshorne was an English scholar in the fields of archaeology, history, and Indology. He was educated at Charterhouse School (~1858–1863) and earned his B.A. from Pembroke College, Oxford (~1864–1868).

Bertram G. Liyanage works in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.A. from Savitribai Phule Pune University, served as a graduate instructor at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and became a PhD student at Temple University (2022).

Beru Khyentse Rinpoche II is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. His traditional teachers include Dzongsar Khenpo Chimey Rinpoche, Kalu Rinpoche, the 16th Karmapa, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Bettina Bäumer works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. Educated at Salzburg, Vienna, Zurich, Rome, and Munich (doctorate ~1967), she has held posts at the Alice Boner Institute, the University of Vienna, and the Abhinavagupta Research Library.

Bettine Birge is a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. She earned her Ph.D. at Columbia University, studying under Wm. Theodore de Bary, Wing-tsit Chan, and Masaaki Sugiyama, and was a visiting scholar at Academia Sinica in 1994.

Indologist and philosopher Betty Heimann studied at Göttingen, Bonn, Kiel (Ph.D.), and Halle. She held posts at Halle, the University of Hamburg, SOAS University of London, and the University of Ceylon (1945–1949).
Betty Jean Shefts is a scholar in linguistics, Tibetology, and Indology. She studied under Franklin Edgerton, Paul Thieme, and Geshe Nornang.
Bhadra Ratna Bajracharya is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He has served as Dean at Lumbini Buddhist University and as Chairman of the Lotus Research Centre.

Linguist and Indologist Bhadriraju Krishnamurti studied at the University of Pennsylvania (A.M., Ph.D.) under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He held academic posts at Andhra University, UC Berkeley, Osmania University (1962–1986), and the University of Hyderabad (1986–1999).
